text: {"score":3,"justification":"Numbers match the card (29.8%, 242, 4.3%, 7.83, 4.87, 22%, 0 documented claims) and the cited claims C0092174 and C0092176 are genuine low-complexity 99215 examples. Tone is cautious. But the headline and leaning of 'inconclusive / too few returned records' undersell a very strong billing-pattern signal (ratio ~7x expected, z 4.87, ~62 excess 99215 claims). The summary gives only two examples, both with 1 condition, and omits the complexity gradient. Next steps are generic and do not name specific claims, even though the exchange returned zero records and the summary says 'what came back is too thin' (it was nothing). An investigator would need to redo some of the analysis.","problems":["Headline frames the case as lack of records and does not state the strong statistical outlier finding up front","Omits the excess 99215 claim estimate (~61.7) and the ratio to expected (~7x), which are on the card","Only two example claims, both 1-condition patients; no 0-condition examples such as C0092287 or C0092390 and no contrast with high-complexity claims","Next steps are generic: no specific claim IDs for the documentation request and no mention of why zero records came back","'What came back is too thin' is imprecise since nothing came back","Does not use the by-complexity table, which shows 99215 share rising from 14% to 56%, to explain billed level versus complexity"]}
